proposals.rationale: Tomahawk is named, and this org's index carries Tomahawk names only at the RDT&E line 0204229N. But the contract maintains a depot FACILITY - depot maintenance, demilitarisation preparation, spares and repairs - paid from fiscal 2018 operations and maintenance (Navy) plus foreign military sales funds. Sustainment and FMS money attached to an RDT&E development line is precisely the appropriation failure mode the rubric flags, and no procurement Tomahawk line exists in this index to carry it instead.

proposals.announcement_evidence: This modification adds scope to procure long lead Group 2, 4 and 10 hardware as well as engineering and program management services in support of Lot 16 production of F-135 propulsion systems
proposals.lexicon_quote: F135 Engine Core Upgrade (ECU)	0604840N	340	F-35 C2D2
proposals.rationale: The only F135 name this org's index carries is the Engine Core Upgrade under F-35 C2D2, a development effort. The announcement is about something else: long lead hardware for Lot 16 PRODUCTION of F-135 propulsion systems, spanning the Marine Corps, Navy, Air Force, non-DOD participants and FMS customers. Linking production long-lead to the ECU development line would be a different-increment substitution, and the multi-service and FMS split means the action is not one Navy line's own work in any case.

proposals.announcement_evidence: Maritime Global Command and Control System Family of Systems Project, and other C2/C4I projects.
proposals.lexicon_quote: Global Command and Control System (GCCS)	2618	333	Navy Command and Control System (NCCS)
proposals.rationale: This is the generic-services pattern of section 3. The award is one of five multiple-award IDIQ contracts for C4I software support and system maintenance - systems engineering, integration, information assurance, training and infrastructure support - to SSC Pacific, and the named program is one of several destinations, the announcement explicitly adding 'and other C2/C4I projects'. Nothing ties the ceiling to the GCCS line's own content, and no task order or obligation is identified at award.

proposals.program_name: The F/A-18 and EA-18G Service Life Assessment Program (SLAP)
proposals.announcement_evidence: to exercise an option to provide depot level maintenance support to facilitate the sustainment of up to 13 F/A-18A-D aircraft.
proposals.lexicon_quote: The F/A-18 and EA-18G Service Life Assessment Program (SLAP)	0702207N	340	Depot Maintenance (Non-IF)
proposals.rationale: Rejected under section 3's platform pattern. F/A-18A-D is the aircraft the option sustains, and the content is depot level maintenance - high flight hour inspections, recurring inspections, modifications and liaison engineering - on up to 13 airframes. The nearest index name is the Service Life Assessment Program, an engineering assessment effort the announcement never mentions; performing depot maintenance is not executing SLAP. No funds are obligated at award.

proposals.announcement_evidence: for the repair and maintenance of the SM-1 standard missile for the governments of Taiwan, Spain, Turkey, Japan, France, Chile, Bahrain, Italy, and Poland
proposals.lexicon_quote: Standard Missiles Mods	2356	342	Standard Missiles Mods
proposals.rationale: The phrase 'standard missile' brushes against this line, but the variant named is SM-1, which this org's index does not carry at all - it carries SM-2 and SM-6. Linking an SM-1 action to the SM-2 mods line would be a variant substitution. The work is also repair and maintenance for nine foreign governments, obligated from foreign military sales funds, so it is neither this line's appropriation nor its own work.

proposals.announcement_evidence: These services are in support of outside the continental U.S. (OCONUS) Task Force Southwest and Marine Corps operations utilizing contractor-owned/contractor-operated MQ-9 unmanned air systems.
proposals.lexicon_quote: MQ-9A	0452	330	Marine Group 5 UAS
proposals.rationale: MQ-9 matches the index designator, but the modification buys nine months of contractor-owned, contractor-operated ISR SERVICES for Task Force Southwest, funded from fiscal 2019 operations and maintenance. The government is buying flight hours, not the Marine Group 5 UAS line's aircraft or kits, so O&M services would be attached to an aircraft procurement line. The MQ-9A name is further carried by both 0452 and 0507 in this index, leaving the owner unresolved.
